speaker: professor
message: Looking at `hash_password()` in `app/auth.py`: What specific risks does using unsalted SHA‑256 pose, and how would adding a salt or using a dedicated password‑hashing library improve security?

speaker: student
message: hash_password is plain sha256 with no salt, so identical passwords give identical hashes and it's fast to brute force; bcrypt or argon2 with a per-user salt would fix it. SECRET_KEY is also hard-coded in auth.py, it should come from an environment variable.

speaker: engineer
message: Looking at `app/db.py`: What happens if two users try to borrow different copies at the exact same time given each request opens its own SQLite connection?
reasoning: Opening a new SQLite connection per request may not sustain thousands of concurrent users, contradicting the README scalability claim.

speaker: student
message: get_connection opens a new sqlite3 connection on every call and never closes it. SQLite only allows one writer at a time, so with many students the writes queue up on the file lock; for real scale I'd move to Postgres with a connection pool.
